platforms.note: Internal web app for the Tecstellar team

challenge: Tecstellar runs several consumer apps — RealBroks and IronDrobe live, Influnet and Vehigo on the way. Users, payments, tickets and follow-ups lived in separate dashboards, one per app, and the calling team worked from spreadsheets.
They needed one console where agents call the right customers, supervisors see who's falling behind and owners see the whole portfolio — without waiting for every app's database to be wired in first.
architectureCaption: One React SPA with three role-based consoles. A store provider picks Firestore or localStorage; TeleCMI dials only in an explicitly allowed mode.

steps.title: Sign in by role
steps.desc: Agents land on today's queue, supervisors on their team, admins on the overview. Per-app permissions decide who can call, see recordings, payments or export.

steps.title: Work the queue
steps.desc: A customer card shows why they're in the queue; the outcome form takes 1–5 for status, Q–I for outcome, Enter to save, S to skip and T to raise a ticket.

steps.title: Call without losing context
steps.desc: The softphone is mounted for the whole session, so a call keeps going while the agent opens history; an ended call waits in the header until it's logged.

steps.title: Escalate and allocate
steps.desc: Mid-call reroutes and escalations land in a live supervisor inbox, and the allocation view shows which languages and states nobody can reach.

steps.title: Audit everything
steps.desc: Every sign-in, access change, approval, payment and export is written to a change log with exactly what changed.

Agents pick which app's queue to work.

Under the hood: role consoles, store provider, Firestore and TeleCMI.

screens.caption: The owner overview: every app's customers, revenue, dues and calls (generated sample data).

decisions.title: Split what TCC owns from what the apps own
decisions.desc: CustomerOverlay is exactly the slice TCC writes (calls, tickets, follow-ups). Customer master data stays the apps'; swapping the sample set for a real fetch touches nothing else.

decisions.title: Two backends, chosen automatically
decisions.desc: With Firebase configured, operational data syncs live across browsers; without it, everything runs in localStorage with zero setup — useful for demos and offline work.

decisions.title: Calling is locked until you mean it
decisions.desc: Sample customers have random numbers, so dialling has three modes: route every call to a test number, dial live, or stay locked with a visible banner.

decisions.title: Keyboard over mouse
decisions.desc: Agents make hundreds of calls a day. Every outcome has a shortcut, so the hands stay on the keyboard between calls.

roadmap: Connect customer master data to the real RealBroks and IronDrobe databases.
Move sign-in to server-side accounts (today it's a demo where only the username is checked).
Bring Influnet and Vehigo onto the console as they ship.
Enterprise TeleCMI features from the spec: recordings at scale and per-agent lines.
